chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who bought food from another man for dirhams, then took half of it, and afterwards came back when the price of the food had risen or fallen, he said: “If, on the day he bought it, he fixed its price with him at such-and-such, then that is the price. But if he had not fixed the price with him, then he is only entitled to the price of that day.”

And he said concerning a man who has two kinds of one foodstuff, and he has priced them similarly while one of them is better than the other, so he mixes them all together and then sells them at one price, he said: “It is not proper for him to do that, deceiving the Muslims by it, unless he makes it clear.”

key_terms.بِدَرَاهِمَ: for dirhams, meaning payment in silver currency
key_terms.سَاعَرَهُ: fixed or agreed a price with him
key_terms.سِعْرُ يَوْمِهِ: the market price of that day
key_terms.طَعَامًا: food commodity being bought and sold
key_terms.لَوْنَانِ: two varieties or grades of the same food
key_terms.يَغُشَّ: to deceive or commit fraud in sale
key_terms.يُبَيِّنَهُ: to make it clear and disclose it to the buyer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on changing market prices after a sale and on mixing different qualities of food in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on sales involving food and pricing. It establishes that an agreed price remains binding, but if no price was fixed, the current market price applies; it also forbids mixing different grades of the same food and selling them without clarification, because that is deception.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3774 - Abdullah ibn Muskan narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (as):

Regarding a man who purchased food with dirhams from another man, took half of it, and then returned later - after the price of the food had either increased or decreased.
Imam (as) said: "If, on the day he purchased it, they agreed on a fixed price, then that price applies. But if no price was fixed, then it is sold at the price of the day it is taken."

Imam (as) also said about a man who had two types of the same food, priced equally, but one was better than the other, and he mixed them together and sold them at one price:
"It is not permissible for him to do that, as it deceives the Muslims, unless he makes it clear (to the buyer)."
